newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines' production indices up in October.
newsitem.headline: Philippines' production indices up in October.

text.p: The Philippines' year-on-year value of production index rose by 6.8 percent in October last year to 452.1, led by the electrical machinery sector, the National Statistics Office reported on Thursday.
On a month-on-month basis, the value of production index dipped by 0.7 percent from September.
The agency said the year-on-year volume of production index increased by 3.8 percent. The month-on-month volume of production index, however, showed a 0.7 percent decline.
Volume of production index is a measure of change in volume adjusted for inflation.

Based on the year-on-year changes in the value of production index, the gainers were electrical machinery, with a 27.4 percent growth; furniture and fixtures, 25.8 percent; and petroleum products, 18.5 percent.
The increased production of electrical machinery can be attributed to microcircuits, electrical wires and batteries, the agency said.
On a volume basis, the winners were iron and steel, 27.2 percent; furniture and fixtures, 26.5 percent; and electrical machinery, 23.4 percent.
The losers on the year-on-year changes in value included wearing apparel at a negative growth rate of 26.0 percent; and rubber products, down 23 percent.

The country's garment industry suffered from lower exports due to stiffer competition from cheaper products of other countries, while the rubber sector had a number of plant closures, the government had previously said.
On a volume basis, wearing apparel and rubber products were also the biggest losers at a negative 34.5 and 21.9 percent respectively.
The agency said the lower value and volume of production on a month-on-month basis were observed in six sectors. Among them were electrical machinery and chemicals.
The agency said these figures were based on the results of its monthly survey of key enterprises in manufacturing.
The October survey covered 422 establishments located mostly in Metro Manila with a response rate of 84.4 percent.
